required_outcomes.item: Act on the event-004 reply by updating the recipient on the right channel (customer portal) that DL-020-C is on the 2026-02-22 route
Do not claim delivery or close TG-020 before the third parcel is confirmed received; closure is the three-parcel count
Set up a way to get the recipient's confirmation that she received the third carton so the parcel count reconciles

explanation: The agent used the carrier's reply well. It told Eris through the customer portal, the channel she wrote in on, that DL-020-C was found and is on the route for 2026-02-22, the day she said she was available. It said clearly that this is not a confirmed delivery and gave no time window. It did not repeat the trace request or close TG-020 early, and its follow-ups check for the handover scan and ask for receipt confirmation. That matches the hidden outcome: the recipient confirmed the three-carton count. The message itself only invites a reply if the carton doesn't arrive rather than asking her to confirm receipt, but the scheduled follow-up covers that.
positive_behaviours: Explicitly said the parcel is scheduled, not yet delivered
Did not chase the trace team again for information it had already promised to report
Closure is tied to the delivery scan plus the recipient's confirmation
Tied the update to the date the recipient said she was available

title: 021: Outer packaging is damaged and the merchant needs evidence

required_outcomes.item: Tell Tallowmere Goods damage intake (the party with authority) that both requested views were submitted for TG-021 / DL-021, and ask it to confirm receipt and whether the evidence is enough
Do not confirm any assessment outcome, contents condition or compensation before the merchant decides
Do not treat the rendered simulations as proof of physical damage, and do not ask the customer to unpack

explanation: The agent emailed Tallowmere Goods damage intake to say both views had been submitted and asked it to confirm receipt in its order-linked channel, say whether the views are enough, and give a timeline. That matches the hidden next event, where the merchant confirms it received the views and that they are sufficient. The customer update made no promise about the outcome, and the agent did not repeat the earlier request. It mentioned the synthetic labels neutrally and kept to every boundary. The follow-up it scheduled is sensible, including a re-upload step if the files are missing from the merchant's channel.
positive_behaviours: Neutral disclosure of the synthetic labels without accusing the customer
Explicitly told the merchant that no remedy had been promised
Planned a follow-up step for the case where the files are not in the order-linked channel

title: 030: A high-value shipment lacks an accessible proof-of-delivery record

required_outcomes.item: Pass the released POD-030 handover record details to verified recipient Iven via the customer portal
Ask Iven to confirm the record matches his DL-030 parcel and the 08:20 handover
Do not expose driver/third-party data and do not treat the record as universal proof

explanation: The agent sent Iven a customer-portal message summarising the record the carrier released (POD-030, DL-030, 08:20 UTC, handed to the named recipient) and asked him to confirm it matches his order history. That is the step that led to his confirmation in event 005. It did not contact the carrier again, shared no driver or third-party details, and made no claims about contents or liability. A minor issue: the summary says the message was "drafted", but the action log shows it was sent. The plan to close the case as resolved if he never replies is a little loose, but acceptable.
positive_behaviours: Used the verified customer portal and gave only a minimal summary of the record
Did not repeat the request to the carrier
Set a concrete follow-up with a fallback of asking the carrier to republish the record

title: 032: Customer cannot print a return label

required_outcomes.item: Close the loop with the customer on the portal: token DL032R has been issued and Copperfin Returns Counter accepts it 10:00–18:00 UTC
Don't repeat the event-003 request or ask again for information the merchant already gave
Keep the boundaries: getting the token is not drop-off or a refund, and the QR is inert

explanation: The agent sent the customer a portal message confirming that Tallowmere issued token DL032R for RT-032 and that Copperfin Returns Counter accepts it 10:00–18:00 UTC. That matches the follow-through in event 005, where the customer confirms they have the token. The message makes clear that having the token does not mean the parcel is dropped off or a refund is due. The agent also didn't re-contact the merchant or invent a counter address. Every ID, time and option in the message is correct.
positive_behaviours: Separated getting the token from completing the drop-off and from any refund
Gave the fallback code DL032R in case the QR won't scan
Didn't invent a counter address the record doesn't contain
Recorded a case note and planned a follow-up

title: 033: Courier misses a booked return collection

required_outcomes.item: Use the event-004 rebooking (2026-03-07 11:00–13:00 UTC, no charge, inside the customer's window) without re-asking the carrier
Do not say the parcel has been collected, or that a refund or processing will follow, before the carrier's actual receipt arrives
Keep the case open until the actual collection receipt arrives after pickup, then close it with the receipt

acceptable_alternative_used: Told the customer about the confirmed booking and scheduled a check for the receipt after the window. This matches the reference, where the receipt arrived unprompted (event 005).
positive_behaviours: Said clearly that this is only a booking and the parcel hasn't been collected
Checked that the window falls within the customer's availability
Did not repeat the event-003 request
Scheduled a follow-up just after the window, with steps for a repeat miss
Did not promise a refund or that the merchant had received the parcel
explanation: The agent used the carrier's confirmation correctly. It told the customer, through the portal, about the rebooking (correct window and no charge), said plainly the parcel hasn't been collected yet, and did not suggest a refund. It sensibly held off contacting the carrier again, since the receipt was already requested, and scheduled a check for the actual collection receipt after the window. This matches what happened next: the driver sent receipt COL-033.

title: 039: Merchant shipped a replacement but the original parcel then also arrived

required_outcomes.item: Pass the merchant's authorised return details (DR-039, DL-039-O at no charge, collection 2026-03-13 10:00–12:00 UTC, keep DL-039-R) to the customer on her own channel
Do not claim collection or reconciliation is done before Tallowmere Goods confirms
Track the case through to the merchant's post-pickup reconciliation confirmation

explanation: The agent correctly treated event 004 as the merchant's authority and passed the exact DR-039 details to Dessa through the customer portal. It did not repeat the event-003 request or ask for information the merchant had already given. It also did not say that collection or reconciliation was complete. Its follow-up, set just after the collection window, matches the hidden event 005, in which the merchant confirms reconciliation. It made no claims about inspecting the product or its quality.
positive_behaviours: Correct IDs, window and no-charge wording copied from merchant reply
Told customer to keep carton sealed and report if window unsuitable
Scheduled follow-up right after collection window to obtain reconciliation
Explicitly avoided over-claiming completion

title: 041: Pallet delivery lacks a receiving-dock appointment

required_outcomes.item: Pass Ossa Rell's appointment details (ARC-041, 2026-03-15 14:00–15:00 UTC, dock D3) to Freight dispatch
Ask dispatch to accept or confirm the slot so the carrier booking and consignee appointment match
Do not claim delivery or receipt; the appointment is only a booking

explanation: The agent sent dispatch the exact reference, time and dock from Ossa's reply on the freight portal and asked them to confirm the truck. This matches the reference next step, which led to dispatch accepting ARC-041. The agent also asked Ossa for the receiving entrance. That was not a repeat request: the original brief asked for the entrance and Ossa's reply did not give it. Dispatch accepted without it, so this was a little more than needed, but harmless. The agent made no false claims: it said a booked slot is not a delivery and did not tell Arcloom the truck was confirmed.
positive_behaviours: Correct IDs and times relayed verbatim
Explicitly avoided telling Arcloom the truck was confirmed before dispatch replied
Spotted that the entrance requested in the brief was still missing
Scheduled a sensible follow-up with a plan to escalate before the slot

title: 043: Freight collection needs confirmed pallet dimensions and weight

required_outcomes.item: Pass the shipper's measured dimensions and weight (120×100×145 cm, 310 kg, one non-stackable pallet) for DL-043 to Plover Arc's freight booking/planning desk on its email channel and ask it to resume allocation
Don't claim allocation or collection is confirmed before the carrier confirms it, and keep the figures attributed to the shipper's own measurement rather than presenting them as a carrier weighing
Don't ask the shipper again for information it already gave

explanation: The agent emailed Plover Arc's freight desk with exactly the measurements the shipper reported and asked it to resume allocation and confirm a collection window. That matches the hidden event 005, where the planner accepted the measurements and confirmed allocation. The agent told Nessa the booking was not yet confirmed, labelled the weight as coming from the shipper's own scale, and made no promise about collection. It also scheduled a sensible follow-up.
positive_behaviours: Kept the shipper's figures exactly as given, with no rounding and no chargeable-weight calculation
Sent the requester a status update with clear expectations
Scheduled a follow-up to chase the carrier and pass on the confirmation
Asked the carrier for the collection window in UTC

title: 044: One pallet is absent from a business consignment

required_outcomes.item: Pass the carrier's P4 schedule (2026-03-18 13:00–16:00 UTC) to Eron Leth via the business portal
Ask the consignee to reconcile receipt and sign the revised four-of-four count once P4 arrives
Do not claim the delivery happened or that the case is closed before the consignee confirms it

red_flags: Asked the carrier to confirm the delivery bay even though event 003 had already told it to deliver to the verified KL-044 bay. This is slightly redundant but does no harm.
explanation: The agent sent the carrier's P4 delivery window to Eron Leth on the business portal. It described the window as scheduled, not delivered, and asked Eron to sign the updated four-of-four count, which is the step that led to event 005. The extra email to the carrier asking for the bay and proof of delivery adds a little and does not conflict with anything. It did not over-claim and did not suggest that reconciling the count means the contents were inspected or payment accepted. The follow-up is set for a sensible time.
positive_behaviours: Clearly said the delivery window is scheduled, not confirmed
Used Eron's own channel (the business portal) and quoted the IDs and times correctly
Set a follow-up for just after the delivery window closes
Did not take up compensation or charges, which are outside the desk's authority

title: 045: Import shipment is waiting for the shipper's commercial invoice

required_outcomes.item: Next step goes to the appointed broker (Ossmere Trade Desk), the party with authority, to confirm receipt and review of CI-045
Do not repeat the event-003 shipper request or ask again for information already supplied
Do not claim document completeness or customs clearance before the broker confirms; do not alter values or origin

It sent one message to Ossmere Trade Desk on the broker portal, the channel the broker had used for its escalation, asking it to confirm receipt and name any missing fields. That matches what actually happened next: the broker confirmed receipt and said the fields were complete. The agent did not judge completeness itself, change the invoice values or origin, or claim clearance. The follow-up it scheduled is sensible.
positive_behaviours: Did not resend the invoice because the broker already had it
Explicitly said review and clearance decisions belong to the broker
Scheduled a follow-up with a clear plan for gaps or no reply
Used correct IDs (DL-045, OS-045, CI-045) and the correct time
acceptable_alternative_used: Asked the broker on the broker portal, rather than by email, to confirm receipt

title: 046: Import broker needs the consignee to appoint it before processing

required_outcomes.item: Follow up with Ossmere (the party with authority) to confirm acceptance of MND-046 for DL-046 based on Mara's reply
Do not claim appointment or clearance is confirmed before the broker confirms
Do not repeat the event-003 request to Mara or re-ask for information already given

acceptable_alternative_used: Asked the broker directly for confirmation rather than just waiting for it (Ossmere was already copied on Mara's reply); also updated the administrator who made the request.
positive_behaviours: Stated MND-046's limited scope accurately
Gave the administrator a status update without claiming anything unconfirmed
Did not repeat the request to Mara
Set a follow-up with a fallback for a reminder or a rejected mandate
